Field guide
Builder's Workshop — blocks & items
27 new placeable blocks, 10 new items and 60 recipes, built on Frontiers without changing terrain generation. Search workshop in the item browser. This content works in existing finite and streamed worlds.
Build connected clear/colored glass panes and iron bars. Place standing or hanging iron/copper lanterns with level-15 light. Chains follow the clicked face axis. Craft hay bales, leather armor, chainmail armor, copper nuggets and pumpkin seeds. Missing light-blue/light-gray stained glass and concrete complete both color sets.
Concrete is a Wildblock wet-mix recipe: 2 sand + 2 gravel + dye + water bucket makes 4 concrete and returns the empty bucket. It does not introduce falling concrete powder. Chainmail uses iron chains in armor patterns; copper oxidation is not added. Glass retains the existing alpha-cutout renderer.
Plant pumpkin seeds on farmland. After 160 simulation seconds, right-click for one pumpkin and restart growth. Break an immature plot for one seed; a mature plot gives a pumpkin and two seeds. This is a regrowing crop-plot adaptation. No new world is required. Existing Frontiers height, streaming and solo-only rules remain.
Frontiers — streamed solo worlds
Choose Infinite-style when creating a NEW world. The active simulation is a rolling 256-block window, not the world boundary: as you travel, new world-coordinate chunks replace distant terrain. Generated base chunks have a bounded 384-chunk cache; block edits and dormant container/entity state are retained separately and included in saves and exports. The generator does not tile a 512-block map.
Terrain uses broad continental, erosion, ridge, river and climate fields, 128-block vertical space, interpolated cave densities, height-based ore veins, biome vegetation, calcite/amethyst geodes and scattered loot ruins. It is Minecraft-inspired, NOT Minecraft's exact generator or matching seeds. It does not reproduce Java's -64..319 height range, aquifers, villages, structures or biome set in full.
This release streams SOLO worlds only. Finite classic worlds retain co-op. No finite save is silently converted. Distant simulations freeze until loaded again; block changes, chest/furnace contents, crops, shapes, water state, drops and entities travel with their world coordinates. Window shifts are synchronous and may pause briefly on slower hardware. View distance is capped at 80 in streamed mode. Unmodified terrain is regenerated rather than saved. Modified-world saves still consume browser storage: export backups, and never clear site data.
Color & Crystal — Overworld update
18 new placeable blocks, four new items and 34 crafting recipes. Smelt all 16 colors of dyed terracotta into patterned glazed blocks. Glazed patterns rotate with your facing on placement and preserve orientation in saved worlds. Search overworld in the item browser to find update content.
New worlds contain calcite-lined amethyst geodes, underground tuff pockets and small emerald deposits in hills. A wooden pickaxe harvests geode shells for four amethyst shards per block; four shards reconstruct one block. Geodes are finite deposits, not a budding-amethyst growth system. Emerald ore needs an iron pickaxe and yields an emerald; emeralds compress into decorative storage blocks, not villager currency in this build.
Golden carrots restore six hunger. Pumpkin pie restores eight; its Wildblock-specific recipe is pumpkin + sugar + wheat, shapeless. Separate saturation and potion effects are not implemented. Tinted glass keeps the existing renderer; Java-exact light blocking is not added.
Existing worlds keep their original terrain. Recipes work in existing worlds, but new natural deposits need a new world. No Nether resources, Nether progression, dimensions or mobs are added. Existing content is preserved. Back up accounts and worlds before updating; do not clear browser site data. Co-op participants must all run this release.
A finite wilderness to mine, build, explore, and survive. All assets used by the game are embedded in this HTML.
Combined edition
This build merges the mod loader and offline Mod Creator with the Java-style Escape menu and thin extruded held-item rendering. Mods are available from the title screen or Options → Mods. Escape pauses gameplay; a second Escape resumes. Modded world saves record required mod IDs and block mappings. Install required packages before importing a modded world. Uploaded mod icons are used in inventory and first-person items; custom block world textures still use the built-in atlas.
Controls
WASD move · Mouse look · Space jump / swim · Ctrl sprint · Shift sneak / edge protection
Hold left mouse: mine · Click left mouse: attack · Right mouse: place / use station / harvest crops
1–9 or wheel: select hotbar · E inventory · F swap main/offhand · Right click held food to eat
F1 toggle HUD · F2 world screenshot · F3 debug information
Q toss one selected item · Ctrl+Q or Shift+Q toss a stack · P save · H guide · Esc pause
Creative only: double-tap Space toggles flight; Space ascends, Shift descends.
Content & crafting completion update
All supported plank families, including mixed woods, now work in generic wooden-tool, crafting-table, stick, chest, bed, bookshelf, shield, and barrel recipes. Matching species are still required for species-specific slabs and oak doors. The # marker in recipe diagrams means an ingredient group, not one particular item. Recipe transfer selects actual owned ingredients, including mixed woods; it does not grant missing items.
Additional materials include more wood families and stripped logs, half slabs, stone variants, copper/lapis/redstone resources, storage blocks, luminous blocks, colored wool and glass, tools, armor, buckets, farming foods, smokers, blast furnaces, barrels, and TNT. Every item is in the JEI-style browser. Left click or R shows recipes; right click or U shows uses; the In-world use tab explains non-crafting behavior. Sources explicitly identify content that is Creative-only in this finite world.
Right-click logs with an axe to strip them. Use shears for leaf blocks, shovels for snowballs, empty buckets to collect source fluids, and flint and steel to ignite TNT. Slabs use actual half-height collision and can combine into full blocks. Carrots and potatoes plant on farmland. Smokers cook food and blast furnaces smelt raw ores at twice normal speed. New generation-3 worlds contain extra tree woods, copper/lapis/redstone ore, deep stone, clay, cane, cactus, mushrooms, pumpkins, and expanded ruin loot. Older saves retain their terrain.
Limitations: no Nether, guardians, ocean monuments, Silk Touch, redstone circuits, fluid spreading, full fire simulation, cocoa farming, or renewable leather. Those resources and limitations are labeled in the item browser rather than represented as fully simulated systems. Snowballs are resources, not throwable projectiles in this build.
New in the previous edition
Ctrl sprints; Shift sneaks slowly with ledge protection. Attacks are click-based: let the meter under the crosshair refill for a strong hit. A fully charged falling attack is critical. Place a shield in the offhand slot; hold right mouse while a sword or shield is selected to block attacks from the front.
Craft a chest from eight matching planks, then right click it for 27 stack-limited storage slots. Craft a bed from three wool above three matching planks; sheep drop wool and mutton. Place the bed on two clear blocks of solid ground. Right click it to set your respawn point; at night it advances to morning if no monsters are nearby. A blocked or broken bed falls back to the original world spawn.
New worlds contain birch groves, meadows, dunes, snowy taiga, and a small ruined structure with supplies. Imported older saves retain their original generator. These are compact biome regions inside the finite world, not Java biome generation. New decorative materials are available in Creative, with survival recipes for chests, beds, shields, wood variants, sandstone, and stone bricks. Some decorative blocks are Creative-only.
Creepers approach quietly and prime when close; back away to stop their fuse. Their explosions damage creatures and optionally terrain. Options can disable creeper terrain damage and adjust field of view, view distance, sensitivity, sound, clouds, and bobbing. Weather alternates between clear skies and rain; rain is visual rather than a full weather simulation. Nights have a star field. F3 shows biome, light levels, and entity counts.
Your first tools
Harvest oak logs by hand. Press E; select a recipe, then click its output to craft. Logs make planks; planks make sticks and a workbench. Place the workbench and right click it for 3 × 3 recipes. A wooden pickaxe requires a workbench. Equip your pickaxe in the hotbar before mining stone and ore. Stone makes cobblestone. Coal needs a wooden pickaxe; iron needs stone; gold and diamond need iron. Tools wear out.
Dropped items & lighting
Mined resources, harvested crops, and pig loot now fall into the world. Walk near an item to collect it after a short pickup delay. Drops tumble, settle, bob and rotate, and nearby matching drops merge. Q tosses one item; Shift+Q tosses the selected stack. Items despawn after five minutes of active world time and are included in saves. Solid walls block pickup attraction.
Separate skylight and block-light grids propagate light through open cells. Solid roofs and walls block light; windows admit light, and leaves and water attenuate it. Torches and burning furnaces emit warm light that spreads around obstacles rather than through solid blocks. Day and night change the sky contribution without switching off torches. This is voxel light propagation and ambient occlusion, not ray tracing or a moving sun-shadow map.
Inventory & crafting
E opens a Java-style player inventory: a live player preview, equipment slots, a 2 × 2 crafting grid, 27 backpack slots, and nine hotbar slots. A workbench opens a 3 × 3 grid. Left click picks up, places, merges, or swaps a stack. Right click takes half a stack or places one item. Shift-click moves between backpack and hotbar, or transfers to an open chest or furnace. Hover a slot and press 1–9 to swap it with that hotbar slot. Hover and press Q to drop one, or Ctrl+Q to drop its stack. Tools have individual durability and do not stack. Equipment must be placed in its actual slot; owning a shield or chestplate in your backpack no longer equips it automatically.
The right-side item browser is inspired by JEI/REI, not the actual Java mods. Left click an item or hover and press R for recipes; right click or U shows uses. Ctrl+F focuses search. Search accepts words, @minecraft, #tags such as #wood, quoted phrases, -exclusions, and | alternatives. A toggles bookmarks; Backspace returns to the previous recipe lookup. Ctrl+O hides the item browser. Recipe ingredients are clickable for nested lookups. The + button transfers owned ingredients into a compatible crafting grid; Shift-click + transfers multiple sets. It never grants missing items. Click the real output to craft onto the cursor, or Shift-click the output to craft into inventory. The browser lists this build’s implemented recipes, not the full 26.3 registry. Middle-click a browser item to obtain a stack in Creative only.
Stacks cap at 64, with tools, shields, beds, and chestplates limited to one. Items that cannot fit remain on the ground. Closing the inventory returns the cursor and unused crafting ingredients to available inventory slots, dropping any overflow safely. Save files preserve slot positions, individual tool durability, equipment, and pending crafting/cursor items. Old Survival inventory counts are migrated into slots; overflow is dropped near you, not deleted. Old Creative saves migrate hotbar contents and use the item browser for the catalog.
Furnaces, food, farming
Craft a furnace from eight cobblestone at a workbench. Right click the placed furnace, insert raw iron, raw gold, pork, sand, or logs, and add coal, logs, planks, or sticks as fuel. Smelting takes time and continues while you play. Hunt pigs or collect apples from leaves; right click held food to eat. Use a selected hoe on grass or dirt to make farmland, then plant seeds. Crops grow over several minutes; right click mature wheat to harvest and replant. Three wheat make bread.
Survival & building
High hunger slowly heals you; sprinting uses more food. Falls, drowning, starvation, and zombies cause damage. Zombies appear in darkness at night and burn during daylight. Torches light nearby surfaces and reduce nearby spawning. An iron chestplate reduces damage when equipped in the chest slot. Right click doors to open or close them. Death respawns you with your inventory preserved, but removes nearby hostile mobs. The day/night cycle lasts twenty minutes.
Saving
Autosave runs every 30 seconds and when paused, if this browser allows local storage for files. Export Save makes a portable JSON backup. Import restores the seed, edits, player, items, furnaces, crops, chest contents, bed respawn point, dropped items, weather, and clock. Keep a backup before creating another world.
26.3 target and scope
Java Edition 26.3 is the project’s target, not a completed compatibility claim. This update implements the requested inventory and a JEI-style recipe browser. It does not add every 26.3 block, item, recipe, entity, world-generation rule, or renderer feature.
Scope
This is an original single-player browser sandbox, not the complete Minecraft game. World size: 128 × 64 × 128. No multiplayer, infinite chunks, dimensions, redstone, enchantments, fluid spreading, every advanced Java inventory gesture, or complete vanilla recipe/mob parity. The backpack now has real stack-limited slots. Advanced drag-distribution, bundles, and the full Java equipment roster are not implemented. The generator and combat are Java-inspired, not exact Java Edition implementations. Creative mode provides blocks and tools, invulnerability, instant mining, and flight. Imported artwork remains subject to its original terms.
Credits and asset terms
Minecraft Bedrock textures, UI artwork, sky and entity skins, and entity geometry from your supplied Mojang Bedrock Samples. Original assets belong to their respective rights holders. This fan-made sandbox is not an official Minecraft product; no affiliation with Mojang or Microsoft. Original asset terms continue to apply.

Multiplayer Unbound — Accounts & Co-op
Personal inventories; shared world and containers. Trusted friends only. Internet is required for PeerJS signaling; GitHub Pages still hosts the game.
Host a world
Create/load a Survival world, then open one room for up to four guests. Keep the host tab awake.
Join a friend
Solo play. Host or join when ready.
Unlock the same account to resume its inventory in the same host world. Room codes are addresses, not passwords. Public PeerJS Cloud/CDN availability and network restrictions can prevent joining; no TURN relay is configured by this game. Signed portable identities; no cloud account recovery or host migration. Export a backup before joining another world.
